title: The 10 Best Transmission Jacks
subtitle: Telescoping and low-profile transmission jacks for home and shop, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A transmission jack holds a transmission level while you unbolt it and lower it out, a job that is dangerous on a floor jack. There are two kinds: telescoping (high-lift) jacks that reach 67 to 74 inches for cars on a lift, and low-profile floor jacks that roll under cars on jack stands. We ranked 10 on star rating, review volume, and features (foot-pedal lift, a tilting saddle, a dual-piston pump, and locking casters).

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: VEVOR Transmission Jack, 1,322 lb Hydraulic Telescoping, High Lift with Foot Pedal
products.verdict: The best-selling telescoping transmission jack on Amazon. It lifts 1,322 lb from about 34 to 68 inches with a foot pedal, for cars on a two-post lift.
pros: 300+ sold a month with a 4.4-star average
Foot pedal raises the load hands-free; saddle tilts up to 30°
Two of the four casters lock; center ring for pushing
cons: The title says 32 to 67 in. but the bullets say 34.3 to 68.5 in.
Needs the car on a lift; it's too tall for jack stands
VEVOR warns the base can be assembled backwards

products.name: VEVOR Hydraulic Transmission Jack, 1,660 lb, 34.6 to 69.3 in. Two-Stage
products.verdict: VEVOR's heavier-duty telescoping jack: 1,660 lb capacity, a tray that rotates 360 degrees and tilts 30, and width-adjustable claws for different transmission pans.
pros: 1,660 lb capacity covers light-truck transmissions and transfer cases
Tray rotates 360° and tilts 30°; mounting plate adjusts in width
Now #2 in Amazon's Transmission Jacks category
cons: About $40 more than the 1,322 lb VEVOR
Newer listing with only about 20 reviews

products.name: JustSmart Dual Plunger Hydraulic Transmission Jack, 1,322 lb, 33.5 to 69 in.
products.verdict: A telescoping jack with a dual-plunger pump that JustSmart says reaches full height in about 20 seconds. It comes with a non-slip pad on the saddle and two safety chains.
pros: Dual-plunger pump lifts faster with fewer pedal strokes
Non-slip NBR pad on the saddle
4.5 stars; two of four casters brake
cons: Priced near the 1,660 lb VEVOR but rated for less weight
Lift time is the seller's claim; we couldn't verify it

products.name: Sunex Tools 7793B 1,000 lb Telescopic Transmission Jack, Foot Pump, Tilt Saddle
products.verdict: The most-reviewed transmission jack we found, from a pro tool brand. It reaches 74 inches, has an overload valve, and lowers far enough to slide the transmission onto a workbench.
pros: 4.6 stars across 220+ reviews
Overload valve stops the jack from lifting beyond its rating
Rams lower enough to transfer the transmission to a work table
cons: About five times the price of the VEVOR
1,000 lb capacity is lower than the imports
Strap tie-down, not chains; only one was left in stock when we checked

products.name: Sunex Tools 7796 1,000 lb Air/Hydraulic Telescopic Transmission Jack with Adjustable Saddle Arms
products.verdict: A shop-grade jack: an air-powered first stage on the foot pedal, a hydraulic second stage on the hand pump, and four ratcheting saddle arms that grab the oil-pan flange.
pros: Air first stage gets the saddle up fast; hydraulic second stage for fine control
Saddle tilts 37° forward, 26° back, and 12° to each side
30.25 in. square base, locking casters, 1-year Sunex warranty
cons: $1,300+; needs shop air regulated to 100 psi
Overkill for a once-a-year job

products.name: Garvee Transmission Jack, 450 lb Low Profile Lift, 7 to 23 in. with Safety Straps
products.verdict: A $94 low-profile jack for cars up on jack stands. It rolls under at 7 inches, lifts to 23, and comes with 2-meter straps to hold the transmission down.
pros: Cheapest jack on the list; 300+ sold a month
7 in. low height fits under cars on jack stands, no lift needed
Four locking casters and two 2 m safety straps
cons: 450 lb capacity: fine for most car transmissions, too little for heavy truck units
No tilt adjustment listed
Tops out at 23 in.; won't reach a car on a lift

products.name: KAFLLA High Lift Hydraulic Transmission Jack, 1,660 lb, 35 to 72 in.
products.verdict: The best value telescoping jack here: 1,660 lb and a 72-inch reach for about $126, with a 4.6-star average across more than 100 reviews.
pros: 4.6 stars, tied with the Sunex jacks for the best rating
1,660 lb capacity and 35 to 72 in. range for about $126
Retaining chain and 30° tilting saddle
cons: The spec table says 1,600 lb while the title says 1,660 lb
Listing doesn't mention locking casters

products.name: MOTOOS 1,100 lb Hydraulic Transmission Jack, 7.68 to 24.8 in. Low Profile Lift
products.verdict: A low-profile jack with more than twice the Garvee's capacity. It rolls under at 7.7 inches and tilts the saddle fore and aft to line up the input shaft.
pros: 1,100 lb capacity in a roll-under jack
Forward and backward saddle tilt for alignment
Works with the car on jack stands

No caster locks mentioned

products.name: VEVOR Transmission Jack, 1,100 lb, 33.5 to 67 in. Two-Stage Telescoping
products.verdict: VEVOR's half-ton telescoping jack: foot-pedal lift, a 30-degree tilting tray, and two safety chains. A cheaper alternative to the 1,322 lb model with a similar review count.
pros: 4.3 stars across about 150 reviews
Two heavy-duty anchor chains secure the load
Foot pedal and pull ring for moving between cars

products.name: LARBANKE Hydraulic Transmission Jack, 1,322 lb, Two-Stage Ram, 33.4 to 68.8 in.
products.verdict: A 1,322 lb telescoping jack with dual-piston pumps for faster lifting, two fixed safety chains, and braking casters, for less than the VEVOR or JustSmart.
pros: Dual-piston pumps need less pedal effort
Two fixed chains on the saddle
About $78 less than the JustSmart dual-plunger jack
cons: Only about 40 reviews
Low stock when we checked

avoid.name: VEVOR Adjustable Floor Transmission Jack, 2,200 lb / 1T Low Profile, 7.28 to 27.6 in.
avoid.flag: Rated half the title's load when moving
avoid.verdict: It's currently Amazon's #1 seller in Transmission Jacks, on the strength of a 2,200 lb headline. The fine print cuts that in half for the way you actually use one, and it costs twice as much as the MOTOOS low-profile jack.
reasons: The title says 2,200 lb, but the first bullet says the transport load is 1,100 lb. A transmission jack spends most of its working life rolling a loaded transmission out from under the car, so 1,100 lb is the rating that matters.
At $330 it costs about twice as much as the 1,100 lb MOTOOS low-profile jack.
The spec table lists its vehicle service type as "ATV" while the title and bullets pitch it for heavy-duty automotive work.
Buyers rate it 2.1 stars, the lowest of any jack we considered for this list.

buyers_guide.a: Telescoping (high-lift) jacks start around 33 to 35 in. and reach 67 to 74 in. They're built for cars on a two-post lift. Low-profile jacks start at about 7 to 8 in. and top out around 23 to 27 in., so they're for cars on jack stands. Pick the one that matches how you lift the car.

buyers_guide.q: How much capacity do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Most car automatics weigh roughly 150 to 250 lb dry, and many light-truck automatics run 200 to 350 lb. A 450 lb jack covers most cars. For trucks, transfer cases, and a margin for torque converter fluid, a 1,000 lb or larger jack is the safer pick.

buyers_guide.q: Can I use a floor jack instead?
buyers_guide.a: Not safely on its own. A floor jack's saddle is small, it rises in an arc, and there's nothing to strap the transmission to. Bolt-on adapter plates exist, but they're usually rated around 300 lb. A real transmission jack has a wide saddle with tilt adjustment and chains.

The transmission's input shaft has to slide straight into the engine's pilot bearing or torque converter. A saddle that tilts forward, back, and side to side lets you match the engine's angle instead of muscling the transmission into place.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a foot pedal?
buyers_guide.a: It helps. With the car on a lift you'll have both hands on the transmission, so a foot pedal lets you raise it without letting go. The telescoping jacks here all use a foot pedal; the low-profile ones use a hand pump.
